title: Date Arithmetic with timedelta
instructions: Use `timedelta` to calculate the difference between two dates and determine a future deadline.
steps: Define two datetime objects: `project_start = datetime(2024, 9, 10)` and `project_end = datetime(2025, 1, 15)`.
Calculate the duration of the project (`project_end - project_start`). Store the result in `duration` and print it.
Define a `timedelta` representing a 45-day extension: `extension = timedelta(days=45)`.
Calculate the new deadline by adding the `extension` to the `project_end` date. Store it in `new_deadline`.
starterCode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

project_start = datetime(2024, 9, 10)
project_end = datetime(2025, 1, 15)

# 1. Calculate duration and print
duration = ...
print(duration)

# 2. Define the extension timedelta
extension = ...

# 3. Calculate and print the new deadline
new_deadline = ...
print(new_deadline.date())
solution:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

project_start = datetime(2024, 9, 10)
project_end = datetime(2025, 1, 15)

# 1. Calculate duration and print
duration = project_end - project_start
print(duration)

# 2. Define the extension timedelta
extension = timedelta(days=45)

# 3. Calculate and print the new deadline
new_deadline = project_end + extension
print(new_deadline.date())
hints: Subtracting two `datetime` objects (`project_end - project_start`) gives you the `timedelta` object.
To calculate the future date, use the addition operator: `project_end + extension`.
The problem asks you to print only the date part of the `new_deadline` object.
